subject: The function choose.files() on OSs other than Windoze

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: The function choose.files() on OSs other than Windoze
parts:
Hi all

If you have used R on Windoze but don't usually do so, you will know
that the very convenient function choose.files only works on Windoze.
While you can of course run R for Windows on Linux (with Wine) or use

tk_choose.files() # from library(tcltk)

I still missed the possibility to not just move around directories
easily and choose more than one file (which tk_choose.files() offers),
but also create a file or even a directory and then also immediately
make that the working directory. For some time I had scribbled
together a function choose.path that did pretty much that, but I
didn't really like how I did that there. I now wrote an at least
slightly better function choose.files that does not rely on other
packages and that I use on Linux. While I have done a bit of testing
myself and didn't immediately run into problems, I'd appreciate any
feedback on it that you might have, e.g., if you find something
doesn't work or if you think a feature is missing (and, you don't have
to write me to only say it's not elegant, I know that myself ;-)). I
put the function on my website for now so if you enter this into R:

source("http://www.linguistics.ucsb.edu/faculty/stgries/
choose.files.r")

then you can use the function much like you can do in Windoze (it
doesn't have the default=... but some other arguments you can play
around with). Like I said, any feedback would be much appreciated and,
if it leads to me changing the code, of course acknowledged.

Cheers,
STG
